shape.text: A legacy key is a lowercase hexadecimal UUID in the 8-4-4-4-12 layout, used before the pcsk_ form and paired with an environment name. Only a third-party secret catalog and one scanner rule describe it, and no provider source states the shape.
The provider documents the key as sent in the Api-Key header and read from PINECONE_API_KEY but states no key grammar; it documents project, index, database and service account identifiers as UUIDs.

issuance.text: New legacy UUID keys can still be issued.

unresolved.reason: Nothing indicates the console still issues UUID keys, and whether they still authenticate is unknown.

collisions.text: A legacy key is lexically identical to the other UUIDs in Pinecone output, such as project, service account and organization identifiers. A UUID under an identifier-named field (PINECONE_PROJECT_ID, X-Project-Id, indexId) is not a key.
As a masking policy and not a provider format, a legacy UUID is treated as a key only when it is the value assigned to a Pinecone API-key name on the same line; a bare UUID is not claimed.

openQuestions.text: Do legacy UUID keys still authenticate, and when did Pinecone stop issuing them?

unresolved.reason: No source says whether legacy UUID keys still authenticate or when Pinecone stopped issuing them.
